Hiccups happen when the diaphragm, the main breathing muscle under your lungs, contracts suddenly and involuntarily. Right after that contraction, the vocal cords close quickly, creating the “hic” sound. Eating too fast can trigger hiccups because you may swallow extra air, stretch the stomach, or irritate nerves that help control the diaphragm. Carbonated drinks, large bites, and sudden temperature changes in food or drink can also contribute. Hiccups usually stop on their own. Slowing your breathing, sipping water, or taking smaller bites next time may help. If hiccups last unusually long, it is reasonable to ask a clinician.
